<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `198703971faf2a5348caeaaa355da5e3c7261216` — the merge of head `6eb78901d530900b1b8ba280817853c171c53d9b` into base `c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 198703971faf2a5348caeaaa355da5e3c7261216 && git checkout 198703971faf2a5348caeaaa355da5e3c7261216
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc 6eb78901d530900b1b8ba280817853c171c53d9b && git checkout -B drift-repro c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc && git merge --no-ff 6eb78901d530900b1b8ba280817853c171c53d9b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c513d62acdd342745bbfe29786ba4b644cd934fc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Delta record: it judges `603928d4a9..1103a1208c` against the findings recorded at `603928d4a9`.
- The head `6eb78901d5` is a sync-only merge of `main`.
- Its tree equals a clean merge of `1103a1208c` with `main`.
- The PR's patch-id against `main` is the same before and after the merge.
- The four PR files are byte-identical between the two heads.

### ① Derived judgments

| Finding | State | Closed by |
|:--|:--|:--|
| M1 | closed | `action-execution.ts:6305-6315`; pins `action-package-addressing.test.ts:2249-2291` (bare route, `_env` address, MCP `run_action`; host code and a plugin) |
| M2 | closed (option 1) | `.changeset/action-route-runs-declared-item-handler.md:13-25`; PR body "What changes" and "Acceptance notes"; docblock `action-execution.ts:6241-6277` |
| S1 | closed | `action-execution.ts:6129`, `6193-6195`, `6297-6300`, `6321-6330`; `action-dispatch.ts:543-549`; pins `test.ts:2294-2321` |
| S2 | closed by statement | `action-execution.ts:6264-6268`, `6328-6330`; changeset line 24; PR body "Acceptance notes" |
| S3 | closed | `action-execution.ts:6211-6236`; `action-dispatch.ts:810-814` |
| S4 | closed | `action-execution.ts:5312-5347` |

- **Doors:** REST bare, `_env`, MCP `run_action` and a host's `dispatchAction` still go through one admitted sequence. The patch adds no second path.
- **Fault path:** a failed store or metadata-service read during attribution answers 503 and runs nothing. Both reads are pinned.
- **Over-refusal:** none introduced, by read. A single holder, a package's action, and a platform action alone dispatch as before.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and correct:
- `@objectstack/runtime: patch`
- BREAKING banner
- one ADR-0087 marker
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`
- `Metadata-protocol: none`
- a `Skills-docs` line in both the body and the changeset

The narrowing's stated extent now matches what is enforced.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev residual (A):** stated under "Not moved" in the changeset and the body. It is a declaration-layer question the maintainer has already ruled on; the follow-up is held by the security seat. Not a blocker.
- **Dev residual (B):** closed for one shared handler under the key. The body's "exactly one shared handler" covers the rest.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing holds against the code it cites and against ADR-0150 D4. The environment's own item runs its own handler or the routing miss. A platform item no longer runs a handler whose environment item is gone.

- **S5 (should-fix, new, not blocking):** a declaration-layer composition. [detail held by the security seat] It is folded into the residual (A) follow-up, not this PR.
- **N1 (nit, carried):** an input shape that no door produces today. [detail held by the security seat]
- **N4 (nit):** the body's wording on the platform route with two shared handlers. Reworded on this head; the body edit moves no code.
- **N5 (nit):** one composition now takes a store read on every dispatch, and it answers 503 during a store outage. This is fail-closed and stated in the body; an operator line in the changeset is a follow-up.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-8fmv`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
